issues.description: Duplicate 'transcriber_error' literal in the error message_type tuple.
issues.detail: The membership tuple lists 'transcriber_error' twice. Runtime-harmless but symptomatic of copy-paste assembly rather than enumerating the documented taxonomy. Deduplicate, and lift the catalog to a module-level frozenset so a set literal would have caught this at write-time.

issues.description: Error-type list is data masquerading as control flow; lift to a named module-level constant.
issues.detail: A fourteen-element tuple inlined into an elif branch tangles the protocol catalog (a value) with dispatch (code). Define ERROR_MESSAGE_TYPES = frozenset({...}) at module scope; the elif becomes 'message_type in ERROR_MESSAGE_TYPES', the duplicate vanishes, and new error codes are a one-line data edit.

issues.description: Collapsed 'Error:' prefix drops per-error-type logging and weakens push_error's observable contract.
issues.detail: Previously auth_error and quota_exceeded had distinct logger.error calls and typed prefixes ('Auth error:', 'Quota exceeded:'). The refactor flattens all fourteen types into one generic 'Error:' string with no logger.error. Restore a single logger.error including message_type, and either keep typed prefixes or pass message_type as a structured field on the error frame.

issues.description: Removing the outer try/except changes failure semantics without documenting the new contract.
issues.detail: The fix is directionally correct — the swallowed disconnect was driving the reconnect-loop wedge — but the new contract ('returns on clean stream end; raises on transport error so the outer reconnect loop drives recovery') is implicit. Document it in a docstring, log once at warning on disconnect before propagating, and audit which iterator exceptions terminate vs. escape.

issues.description: Inner bare 'except Exception' still swallows transport errors and conflates failure modes.
issues.detail: The remaining try/except inside the async-for catches parse errors, dispatch errors, and downstream handler errors as one log line, and may also catch transport-level exceptions mid-iteration — re-introducing the very swallow this PR set out to fix. Narrow the except to handler-domain exceptions or re-raise transport errors after logging.

issues.description: Changelog file is missing a trailing newline.
issues.detail: changelog/3233.fixed.md ends with '\ No newline at end of file'. Trivial, but POSIX text-file convention and downstream changelog concatenation tools depend on it. One-byte fix worth doing for hygiene.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the fix is directionally correct: the outer try/except in _receive_messages was swallowing websocket disconnect exceptions and wedging the reconnect loop, and removing it is the right shape. Execution is sloppy, however. The error-type expansion is assembled by copy-paste — 'transcriber_error' appears twice, the fourteen-element tuple is inline data tangled with dispatch, per-type logging and typed error prefixes are silently dropped, and the new exception-propagation contract on _receive_messages is not documented. Lift the error catalog to a module-level frozenset, restore typed per-error logging, document the receive-loop contract, narrow the inner except, and fix the changelog newline. Then it lands.
